text:
simon: Quick FYI — I'm going to land a small TF change to add a surge throttle on the new gpu-nodepool and annotate namespaces with a quota label so the autoscaler doesn't overfill pods in low-priority namespaces. Would love a quick security/secret-path check before I merge.

maria: thanks — can you paste the diff? want to make sure HPA targets and VPA won't fight the throttle.

simon: paste below. it's just a new module var + node pool scaling config.
```hcl
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "./modules/node_pool"
  name   = "gpu-surge"
  surge_limit = 2 # hard cap on concurrent surge nodes
  max_nodes   = 40
}
resource "kubernetes_namespace" "ml-inference" {
  metadata {
    name = "ml-inference"
    annotations = {
      "redwood/scale-quota" = "low-priority"
    }
  }
}
```

elaine: :eyes: that surge_limit is fine, but we should be explicit about pod disruption budgets and eviction thresholds. Also, where is the node pool credential coming from? the service account path changed last sprint.

simon: good call. TF uses secret path `vault/data/infra/nodepools/gpu` which I updated in the vars. old path was `vault/data/infra/nodepools`. cc @kevin for secret rotation impact.

kevin: confirmed — the new path is ok for infra-ops, but make sure the k8s service account referenced by the autoscaler has the right IAM role. autoscaler logs will show 403s otherwise.

maria: about HPA/VPA — most inference deployments use CPU-based HPA with targetUtilization ~60 and VPA in "recommendation" mode. The throttle won't break that, but if VPA starts recommending more CPU and HPA scales up pods, node surge cap can cause pending pods. we should add a fallback policy: if pending pods > 5 for 2m, route traffic to the dedicated pool.

simon: yeah we have a smart routing policy but not wired for this namespace yet. I'll add a canary route in the scale policy. sample alert rule I plan to add:
```yaml
- alert: NodeSurgePendingPods
  expr: kube_pod_status_phase{namespace=~"ml-.*",phase="Pending"} > 5
  for: 2m
  labels: {severity: "page"}
  annotations: {summary: "Pending pods > 5 due to node surge limit"}
```

elaine: also add an annotation to the namespace so ops can opt-out of the throttle: `redwood/scale-exempt=true`. We may need to exempt perf test namespaces.

kevin: small nit on TF: when you change the vault path, run `terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars` locally and check `vault kv get -format=json` output; we'll have a CI check soon to validate secret paths.

infra-bot: deploy-check: terraform plan succeeded in sandbox (plan id: tb-2211). 2 resources to add, 1 to change.

maria: thanks infra-bot — can you drop the plan output link?

infra-bot: https://ci.redwood/prod/plans/tb-2211

simon: putting up PR: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/pulls/842 — includes node pool surge_limit, namespace annotation, and the routing alert. requesting review from @elaine and @kevin.

elaine: LGTM with 2 comments inline about PDBs and eviction thresholds. will approve after those. :thumbsup:

kevin: I checked IAM mapping, no changes required. approve once you add the fallback route and a short blurb in the runbook.

maria: agree, add runbook steps: how to temporarily remove the surge cap and how to toggle `redwood/scale-exempt`.

simon: thanks all — I'll patch the PR and ping again. If nobody raises a blocker by EOD, I'll merge and coordinate a short canary deploy to staging.

maria: sounds good.

elaine: thanks, will follow the staging canary.

kevin: :ok_hand:
